objective: Add explicit point-in-time hard financial and delisting risks to the existing Shanghai/Shenzhen dynamic tradable universe and compare it with the unfiltered base universe and CSI300 under a next-session executable timing convention.

base_universe.base: all historically listed Shanghai and Shenzhen A shares

execution.note: Next-session close is conservative and executable; later production work may replace it with next-open or VWAP.

benchmarks: each strategy is compared with the next-session equal-weight benchmark of its own point-in-time universe
pre_registered_questions: How many otherwise tradable securities are removed by each hard-risk reason?
Does the hard-risk overlay reduce drawdown or tail loss without materially destroying own-universe excess return?
Does the conclusion hold in both pre-existing subperiods?
How does the hard-risk version compare with CSI300 under the same next-session timing?
forbidden_actions: add ROE profit growth PE PB or cash-flow-quality thresholds after viewing returns
change severe audit patterns after viewing returns
block missing financial data after viewing returns
add market-cap filters or change ADV threshold after viewing returns
change factor signs family weights top_k dates or execution timing after viewing returns
treat retrospective results as true forward evidence
approve live trading from this experiment
